LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD packages a prebuilt AppImage release of Actual Budget, a local-first personal finance tool. The sources come from the project's own official GitHub releases (`github.com/actualbudget/actual`) and `raw.githubusercontent.com` for the LICENSE file, all pinned to a specific version tag (`v26.9.0`). All sources have proper SHA256 checksums (not `SKIP`), which is good practice for a binary distribution package.

The `prepare()` function performs standard AppImage packaging operations: making the AppImage executable, extracting its squashfs contents with `--appimage-extract`, verifying the Electron version (informational only), substituting template variables in the launcher script via `sed`, cleaning up prebuilt node modules for other architectures, and renaming the desktop/metainfo entries. The `package()` function installs files into the standard Arch filesystem locations (`/usr/bin`, `/usr/lib`, `/usr/share/applications`, `/usr/share/metainfo`, `/usr/share/icons`, `/usr/share/licenses`) — all routine packaging operations.

There are no signs of malicious behavior: no `curl|bash` patterns, no `eval` of decoded blobs, no base64-encoded payloads, no data exfiltration, no unexpected network endpoints, and no tampering with files outside the package's scope. The launcher script (`actual.sh`) is not included in this file but is pinned by SHA256, so it would be verified separately when building the package.

Minor hygiene notes (not security concerns): the package installs prebuilt binary artifacts from the upstream vendor, which inherently requires trusting Actual Budget's release pipeline, and the launcher script is a separate file in the AUR repo (standard for `-bin` packages of this style).
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard PKGBUILD packaging prebuilt Actual Budget AppImage from official upstream with proper checksums.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for actual.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a legitimate shell script for running the "actual" Electron application on Arch Linux. It sets up environment variables (ELECTRON_IS_DEV, NODE_ENV, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, etc.) and handles desktop environment compatibility for Electron's trash implementation. The script loads user-defined flags from XDG config files in a standard pattern, applies sandbox restrictions only when running as root without ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, and ultimately executes the electron binary with collected flags. 

The template variables (@appname@, @runname@, @electronversion@) are standard AUR packaging placeholders replaced during installation. There are no network requests, no downloads, no obfuscated code, no eval/base64 execution, and no suspicious system modifications. The flag-loading loop reads from configured XDG paths and skips comments/empty lines, which is normal application configuration behavior. The --no-sandbox guard is properly conditional on EUID and ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE. All operations are consistent with standard Electron application packaging and do not exfiltrate data, install backdoors, or execute attacker-controlled code.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Legitimate Electron app launcher with no malicious patterns
</summary>
</security_assessment>
